entities.summary: Sebastian Maggi (1414–1496) was an Italian Roman Catholic priest and a professed member of the Dominicans. He served as the confessor to both Girolamo Savonarola and Catherine of Genoa. Maggi was born in unknown, but his early life and education are not well-documented. He became a prominent figure in the Dominican Order, known for his spiritual guidance and intellectual pursuits. Maggi's significance extends beyond his individual influence, as he played a role in shaping the spiritual landscape of Italy during the late Middle Ages. His legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Dominican Order and the impact of his teachings on the spiritual development of his contemporaries.
